problem: Robot long-term memory systems built on categorical/metric maps have closed vocabularies, and open-vocabulary pipelines like ReMEmbR caption frames into text (captioning bottleneck), losing fine-grained visual details (small/secondary objects, texture, layout). Feeding whole videos to a VLM does not scale in cost or context.
motivation: Lifelong deployment needs a compact, scalable memory that keeps fine visual semantics and is grounded in space and time. Modern multimodal embedders are aligned with text well enough to be indexed directly in vector databases, so captions may be unnecessary.
key_idea: Store frame-level multimodal visual embeddings together with pose and timestamp in a vector database, and let a tool-using VLM agent iteratively retrieve by text, time, position or image to answer queries and output goal coordinates for A* navigation.
insight: Skipping captioning preserves details that captions miss; the gap over ReMEmbR widens from ~13% on simple queries to ~30% on hard ones, and ReMEmbR failures are traced to under- and over-captioning. Retrieval shortens the VLM's working context: with 27B-32B open VLMs, VLM-Only collapses (e.g. 11-14%) while RAVEN keeps 55-68%, and 250x sparsification costs only ~10% accuracy. Design ablations show that including similarity scores and a larger top-K help, and that forward-chronological ordering of time retrieval (49.0%) beats centered (32.65%) and nearest-neighbor (42.86%) ordering on FindingDory ep_1.
method: Visuo-spatio-temporal memory: each frame is encoded by a pretrained multimodal embedder (QQMM-v2, Seed1.6-Embedding, SigLIP, CLIP) and stored as (pose, timestamp, embedding, image) in a FAISS/Milvus vector DB with sub-linear top-K search.

Four retrieval tools: text-based (cosine between the encoded agent-written query and the stored embeddings), time-based (consecutive memories from a timestamp), position-based (spatial nearest neighbors), and image-based.

Agentic loop: a VLM keeps working context R_tau, decides whether the evidence is enough, otherwise calls a tool; retrieved entries are appended (R_{tau+1} = R_tau ∪ retrieved). It exits with a text answer, a spatial goal (x,y,z), or a time reference. Max 3 tool calls (15 for FindingDory).
Retrieval-response design: similarity scores are shown to the VLM as a confidence cue, and time-based retrieval returns memories in forward chronological order starting at the target timestamp.

Robot pipeline: on a Unitree Go1 with ZED 2i RGB-D SLAM and a Jetson Orin NX, greedy frontier exploration builds the memory and a 2D occupancy map; the predicted goal is then followed with A* and a PD controller, with no further exploration.
Training-free and plug-and-play: only pretrained embedders and VLMs are used, and the memory is compact (22,315x smaller than raw RGB; ~90% performance at 0.12 fps and 250x sparsification).

setting.backbone: Frozen VLM agents (Gemini-2.5-Flash/Pro, Gemini-3-Pro, GPT-4o, GPT-5, GPT-5.2, Gemma3, Qwen-VL) + frozen multimodal embedders (QQMM-v2 8.3B, Seed1.6-Embedding, SigLIP, CLIP)
setting.model_size: Embedders from 150M (CLIP-B) to 8.3B (QQMM-v2); VLMs 7B-32B open and frontier closed
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB video frames with depth, pose and timestamps (RGB-D SLAM on the robot)
setting.action_space: Predicted (x,y,z) goal, then A* waypoints tracked by a PD controller on a quadruped
setting.simulator: Habitat (FindingDory and 19 RAVEN-QA scenes); NaVQA is based on the real CODa dataset
setting.privileged: none at query time; the memory is built beforehand by exploration, and the 2D occupancy map is reused for planning. Objects missed during exploration cannot be retrieved.

The paper's own benchmarks (RAVEN-QA splits) and NaVQA/FindingDory are not among the canonical benchmark names, so they are listed as 'other:'. The split labels 'test' and 'val' are best guesses. NaVQA rows for other VLMs are in the appendix table.
results: With Gemini-3-Pro on NaVQA, RAVEN (QQMM-v2) reaches 76.2/52.6/80.0 descriptive accuracy with the lowest short/medium positional error (2.37 m / 11.48 m), beating the ReMEmbR variants on most metrics. On FindingDory's long subset it beats VLM-Only (32.2 vs 28.2) while retrieving only 7.43% of memory, but on the full set VLM-Only is higher (38.2 vs 35.1). On real-world robot tasks RAVEN reaches 92.38% (Gemini-2.5-Flash), against 76.67% for ReMEmbR and 85.24% for VLM-Only, and it stays far ahead of both with open VLMs.
limitations: Retrieval quality is bounded by the pretrained embedder's alignment, and there is no domain-specific fine-tuning.
Memory is a static database: it cannot handle dynamic scenes and has no update or pruning mechanism.

Objects missed during exploration cannot be retrieved. Frontier VLMs with full context (VLM-Only) sometimes match or beat RAVEN, e.g. FindingDory full and Habitat with Gemini-3-Pro. Medium open VLMs (27-32B) often do no better than the embedder-only baseline.
